title: Cap. IV Arg. 5 Sol cont: benevolence toward elect still in sin — Orange 25; Scotus; two acceptations
pass_a_gloss: Further, what they say, That God makes or holds no one pleasing in Christ except a faithful one, can in no way stand. For I ask, Whence is born the efficacious purpose in God of inspiring saving faith and repentance into human hearts? In this very purpose which still regards unbelievers and the impenitent, it is necessary that they acknowledge a certain singular and special love of God. For so great is God's love toward his only-begotten Son, that in view of him with the love of eternal benevolence he embraces all those whom he elected in him, even considered in the state of sin and unbelief; and therefore by a certain special grace he always cares that they be drawn out of this state. Most clearly to this sentence the Council of Orange, Displeasing we were loved, that there might be made in us whence we might please, can. 25. To these add, that Christ is a head of such infinite power, and his merit of such efficacy, that he can influence into members not yet united, but only destined, and by his influence bring it about that such be united. This is that which Scotus well observed, book 3 distinction 19. Christ merited that things not joined to him should be joined: and in this chiefly consists his merit. If Christ's merit reaches to the non-joined, that is, non-believers, and brings it about that they be joined, then also a certain conforming acceptance or gratifying of God is extended to the same. More briefly therefore I answer, That a man can be said to be acceptable to God in Christ, or for Christ's sake, in two ways. In one way, when he embraces him with a love as of present friendship, and admits him as a household member to the throne of grace, and blesses him with the sense of his favor. In this sense only the faithful are pleasing to God in Christ. In another way someone can be understood to be pleasing and acceptable to God before others, namely, when he embraces him with the love of eternal benevolence, as a predestinated member of his Son. For although the effects of paternal love are not yet poured out upon such a one, he nonetheless intends in Christ and for Christ's sake to pour them out at a fit time. And in this sense God has made many even not yet believing and converted pleasing to himself in Christ, not as already placed in Christ, but as to be placed by special favor, because elected in Christ from eternity.
pass_b_english: Further: their claim that God makes or holds none pleasing in Christ except the faithful cannot stand. Whence comes God's efficacious purpose to inspire saving faith and repentance into human hearts? That purpose still regards unbelievers and the impenitent — so they must grant a singular, special love of God there. So great is his love for his only-begotten Son that, looking to him in eternal benevolence, he embraces all he elected in him even while considered in sin and unbelief — and by special grace always works to draw them out of that state. So Orange can. 25: Displeasing we were loved, that there might be made in us whence we might please. Add: Christ is a head of infinite power, his merit of such efficacy that it can influence members not yet united but only destined, and by that influence unite them. Scotus (3 dist. 19) well noted: Christ merited that the not-yet-joined be joined — and therein his merit chiefly consists. If his merit reaches non-believers and joins them, a conforming divine acceptance extends to them too. Briefly: one may be acceptable to God in Christ, or for Christ's sake, two ways. One: present friendship-love, admitted as a household member to the throne of grace — in that sense only the faithful are pleasing in Christ. Two: eternal benevolence as a predestinated member of his Son — though paternal effects are not yet poured out, he intends in Christ and for Christ to pour them at the fit time. In that sense God has made many not yet believing or converted pleasing in Christ — not as already placed in him, but as to be placed by special favor, because elected in Christ from eternity.
source_text: Porro, quod dicunt, Deum neminem in Christo gratum facere aut habere nisi fidelem, id nullo modo potest consistere. Quaero enim, Unde nascitur efficax propositum in Deo, inspirandi fidem salutiferam et poenitentiam cordibus humanis? In hoc ipso proposito quod spectat adhuc infideles et impoenitentes, singularem ac specialem quendam Dei amorem agnoscant est necesse. Tantus enim est Dei amor erga Filium suum unigenitum, ut ejus intuitu amore aeternae benevolentiae complectatur eos omnes, quos in illo elegit, etiam in statu peccati et infidelitatis consideratos; et propterea speciali quadam gratia curat semper eos ex hoc statu eruendos. Praeclare in hanc sententiam Concilium Arausicanum, Displicentes amati sumus, ut fieret in nobis unde placeremus, can. 25. Hisce adde, Christum esse caput tam infinitae potentiae, ejusque meritum tantae efficaciae, ut influere possit in membra nondum unita, sed solummodo destinata, et suo influxu efficere ut talia uniantur. Hoc illud est quod Scotus bene observavit, lib. 3. dist. 19. Christus meruit ut non conjuncta sibi conjungerentur: et in hoc potissimum consistit meritum ejus. Si Christi meritum ad non-conjunctos, hoc est, non-credentes, pertingit, efficitque ut conjungantur, tum etiam et conformis quaedam Dei acceptatio sive gratificatio ad eosdem extenditur. Brevius itaque respondeo, Hominem aliquem dici posse Deo acceptum in Christo, vel propter Christum, dupliciter. Uno modo, quando illum complectitur amore quasi praesentis amicitiae, illumque ut domesticum ad thronum gratiae admittit, atque sensu favoris sui beat. Hoc sensu soli fideles sunt in Christo Deo grati. Alio modo intelligi potest aliquis esse prae aliis Deo gratus et acceptus, nimirum, quando illum complectitur amore aeternae benevolentiae, ut praedestinatum Filii sui membrum. Licet enim adhuc paterni amoris effecta ad talem non defundantur, intendit tamen in Christo et propter Christum idoneo tempore diffundere. Et hoc sensu Deus multos etiam nondum credentes et conversos gratos sibi fecit in Christo, non tanquam jam positos in Christo, sed tanquam ex speciali favore ponendos, quia ab aeterno in Christo electos.
